what: highlight "no depositor has ever lost a penny of FDIC-insured funds"
said: There is one sentence the United States government is very proud of. Since nineteen thirty-three, no depositor has ever lost a single penny of insured money.

what: highlight "WaMu's closure and receivership is the largest bank failure in American financial history"
said: And yet, American banks fail. Sometimes huge ones. In two thousand eight, a bank with three hundred billion dollars in assets collapsed in a single week.

what: highlight "Bank reserves are held as cash in the bank or as balances in the bank's account at the central bank ."
said: The bank keeps a small part of it as reserves. Those are cash in the bank, or money in the bank's own account at the central bank.

what: highlight "in which banks would keep all depositor funds on hand as reserves"
said: This system is called fractional-reserve banking. Fractional means the bank keeps only a fraction, a part, of its deposits on hand.

what: highlight "do not impose explicit reserve requirements at all"
said: Here is something that surprises people. The United States does not even require banks to keep a set minimum anymore.

what: highlight "only a proportion of deposits will be withdrawn at the same time"
said: Why does this work most of the time? Because on a normal day, only a few customers take money out. The bank keeps enough for normal days.

what: highlight "while loans made by banks tend to be longer-term"
said: But there is a built-in problem. Deposits can be taken out any day. Loans take years to pay back.

what: highlight "the central bank may provide funds to cover the short-term shortfall as lender of last resort"
said: On a bad day, a bank can borrow from other banks for a short time to cover a gap. In a real emergency, the central bank can lend to it too. That is called being the lender of last resort.

what: highlight "it may become a self-fulfilling prophecy"
said: Economists call this a self-fulfilling prophecy. The fear itself causes the thing it fears.

what: highlight "mentioned bank runs as a prime example of the concept"
said: The sociologist who invented the phrase self-fulfilling prophecy used bank runs as his main example.

what: highlight "it is logical for individual depositors to engage in a bank run once they suspect one might start"
said: Two economists, Diamond and Dybvig, showed why. Once you think a run might start, the smart thing for you is to run too, even if the bank was healthy.

what: highlight "Many of the recessions in the United States were caused by banking panics."
said: When many banks have runs at the same time, it is called a banking panic. America had a lot of them.

what: highlight "Banking panics began in the Southern United States in November 1930"
said: The worst ones came after the nineteen twenty-nine stock crash. In November nineteen thirty, a string of banks in Tennessee and Kentucky collapsed, and panic spread.

what: highlight "declared an eight-day bank holiday"
said: By February nineteen thirty-three, things were so bad that Michigan closed all its banks for eight days. Within weeks, every state did the same.

what: highlight "he declared a four-day national banking holiday"
said: Delaware was the last state to close its banks, on March fourth. On March sixth, the new president, Franklin Roosevelt, closed every bank in the country.

what: highlight "FDR gave his first fireside chat"
said: Congress passed an emergency law three days later. On March twelfth, Roosevelt went on the radio and explained it in plain words to the whole country.

what: highlight "allowed the twelve Federal Reserve Banks to issue additional currency"
said: The new law let the Federal Reserve print extra currency for banks that reopened, so they could pay anyone who came to the counter.

what: highlight "depositors stood in line to return their stashed cash to neighborhood banks"
said: The next morning, when banks reopened, something amazing happened. People stood in line to put their cash back in.

what: highlight "are seen to have ended the bank runs that plagued the Great Depression"
said: Historians now see that bank holiday as the moment the runs of the Great Depression finally ended.

what: highlight "The FDIC was created by the Banking Act of 1933"
said: On June sixteenth, nineteen thirty-three, a new law created the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the FDIC.

what: highlight "covers up to $250,000 per depositor, per FDIC-insured bank, for each account ownership category"
said: Today, the limit is two hundred fifty thousand dollars per depositor, per bank, for each type of account ownership.

what: highlight "Each ownership category of a depositor's money is insured separately up to the insurance limit"
said: Ownership type means things like an account in your own name, a joint account with a spouse, or certain retirement accounts. Each is counted separately.

what: highlight "for total insurance coverage of $1,500,000"
said: So one person with three types of accounts at two different banks could be covered for up to one and a half million dollars.

what: highlight "backed by the full faith and credit of the government of the United States"
said: The insurance is backed by the full faith and credit of the United States government. That means the whole country stands behind it.

what: highlight "The FDIC charges premiums based upon the risk that the insured bank poses."
said: Who pays for it? Mostly the banks themselves. They pay the FDIC insurance premiums, and riskier banks pay more.

what: highlight "Non-US citizens are also covered by FDIC insurance"
said: You do not even have to be an American citizen. The insurance covers anyone with deposits at an insured bank's office inside the United States.

what: highlight "Stocks , bonds , and mutual funds including money funds"
said: But not everything at a bank is insured. Stocks, bonds and mutual funds are not covered, even if you bought them through your bank.

what: highlight "with 2,239 retail branch offices operating in 15 states"
said: In September two thousand eight, Washington Mutual was the largest savings bank in America. It had more than two thousand branches in fifteen states.

what: highlight "WaMu had total assets of $307 billion"
said: It had more than forty-three thousand employees and over three hundred billion dollars in assets.

what: highlight "the withdrawal of US$16.7 billion in deposits during a 9-day bank run"
said: After its credit rating was cut, customers pulled out sixteen point seven billion dollars in just nine days.

what: highlight "seized WaMu's banking operations and placed them under the receivership"
said: On September twenty-fifth, regulators seized the bank and handed it to the FDIC.

what: highlight "The FDIC sold the banking subsidiaries"
said: Then the FDIC sold the banking business to JPMorgan Chase, for about two billion dollars. Customers simply became JPMorgan Chase customers.

what: highlight "WaMu filed suit against the FDIC"
said: The bank's owners were so upset that they later sued the FDIC, claiming the bank had been seized unfairly and sold too cheaply.

source: Wikipedia, Collapse of Silicon Valley Bank
what: highlight "customers had withdrawn $42 billion"
said: Fifteen years later, it happened again, faster. In March twenty twenty-three, Silicon Valley Bank lost forty-two billion dollars in deposits in one day.

source: Wikipedia, Collapse of Silicon Valley Bank
what: highlight "Employees received their annual bonuses on March 10, 2023, hours before the government took control of the company."
said: One detail made many people angry. The bank's employees received their yearly bonuses on March tenth, just hours before the government took control.

source: Wikipedia, Collapse of Silicon Valley Bank
what: highlight "all depositors would have full access to their funds the next morning"
said: Two days later, the government made a special decision. Every depositor, insured or not, would get full access to their money the next morning.

what: highlight "deposited $30 billion with First Republic"
said: A few weeks later, another bank wobbled. Eleven of America's biggest banks put thirty billion dollars into First Republic Bank to calm the panic.

what: highlight "the FDIC announced that First Republic had been closed and sold to JPMorgan Chase"
said: It was not enough. On May first, regulators closed it, and JPMorgan Chase bought nearly all of it.

what: highlight "paying the FDIC $10.6 billion for nearly all of First Republic's assets"
said: JPMorgan paid the FDIC ten point six billion dollars for nearly all of it. The biggest bank in America got even bigger.

what: highlight "the FDIC is appointed receiver"
said: Rosa's bank is closed by regulators. The FDIC is appointed to take over. In bank language, it becomes the receiver.

what: highlight "in which deposits (liabilities) are assumed by an open bank"
said: The FDIC has two main ways to handle a failed bank. The most common one is to find a healthy bank that will take over the deposits and buy the loans.

what: highlight "Deposit payoff"
said: If no bank wants it, the FDIC pays depositors directly, up to the insured limit. That is called a deposit payoff.
